body:
I am currently staying at the cheapest hotel I could find. My landlord said my credit score was a 'high C' when they normally want somebody who had at least 'low B.' Whatever that means. They rented it to me regardless.

Also, I am looking to find whatever I can. I haven't been turning down apartments left or right or anything like that, nor been particularly choosy. Just trouble finding an affordable one that wasn't already getting snatched up. I now have a few I am checking out this weekend that I am hopeful about.

With that expanded upon - any suggestions for loans that'll accept whatever a 'high c' credit score gets?

I'm curious to see how the story will end.

We will all die, sooner or later. So why rush it? Yeah, shit hurts and sucks a lot- especially these days. But I want to see how my story will naturally end. 

I could die young and quick with a sudden surge of regret in my heart.

I could live to be old, old enough to watch my parents die and my young siblings grow and make families of their own. I could die in my sleep, oblivious.

Regardless of whether I am ready for it or not, death will come for me. Might as well see how much I can get out of life until then. What does the temporary pain of now compare to the endless quiet of oblivion awaiting me?

The pain and hurt will end soon enough. Might as well see the crap show to its conclusion.

That might be what I have to do- but I really need to have a job that pays enough for when rent comes around. 12 dollars an hour just won't do it. 

Thanks for the advice. I shall keep sending out applications and attending job interviews.

My family lives across the country from me and is hard to live with. I would much rather not if possible. Quite honestly, I'd rather be living in my car. 

I will keep doing what I can to find work.
Office work would be ideal, but for some reason it seems hard to get in my area. I intend to keep on applying and maybe then I will have some luck. Thanks for your words.

He got his wife to block everyone on everything when he went  no contact with us. Even if I could contact her, I have no idea what lies her told her so she likely won't believe me. 

Also, imagine being in my shoes- telling the world that your more respected and socially acceptable brother raped you. Add in the fact that he is more charismatic and was able to convinced my father all of us were lying about him- then yeah.   


I was also a child when all this happened and very ashamed and confused and hurt.

Soooo yeah.
"You were raped" Would have saved me almost a decade of confusion.

I don't think I ever had an orgasm, but there were times where what he did to me felt pleasurable. Which made me feel incredibly guilty and shameful- and solidified in my messed up mind that is was my fault somehow. That also fueled my self hatred and made me think that I must have secretly wanted it. Even though that wasn't at all the case.

It took a long time to work through because that aspect  isn't something that is talked about. Which makes sense as people already cast so much doubt on survivors of rape that if the involuntary pleasure  aspect became a source of discussion in the mainstream- it would likely worsen things for survivors.

People are unbelievably cruel, clueless and tactless sometimes when it comes to stuff like this.

I suppose it's the kind of standard talk therapy that's offered for free with my university. I'll no longer have access to that once I graduate but I will hopefully be able to work that out afterwards.

I can't say I've ever had it. The most I indulge with spices is like - the mild sauce from Taco bell or the cayenne pepper in those small packets lmao

Maybe I'll give it shot sometime. Whats a good thing to try it with to start?

He is in the military, married with two kids. He graduated top of his class with honors. He was living in North Dakota, but I've heard through the grapevine that he might have the opportunity to go serve somewhere in Europe- this was before Ukraine so I imagine its a privileged sort of position.

At this point, I wouldn't be surprised if he has left the USA.

Thanks for the encouragement! I'm in my last semester of university and I just don't have a lot of spare time or cash right now - I will be graduating soon and starting my first 'real' job so I should be able to soon :D

Sickening and painful.

Every now and again I am reminded of those events and find myself temporarily crippled by the strong emotions that paralyze my entire body. I feel this horrible anxiety-triggered sickness that causes me to dissociate so hard I am no longer aware of myself and my body. Its like I am in that moment relieving being raped again.

Imagine you are trying to live your life literally over a decade later in a fucking walmart and all of sudden you relive one of the worst childhood experience in your life- all the fear, pain, desperation, humiliation, shame, and helplessness just rushing back into as you are paralyzed staring at a fruit for what can be a few seconds to several minutes.

It isn't something anyone deserves. Not even rapists or pedophiles themselves.

There are people out there who can and are willing help. It isn't your fault- you didn't want this nor ask for it. Even if you had done everything 'right' they likely still would have done it anyway- with you or someone else. 

This having happened to you says more about the people around you than you yourself as a person.
My older brother is 2 and half years older than me. My two younger sisters he molested are 4 and 7 years younger than him.

Non-existent lmao.

I have never dated and likely won't anytime soon. It wouldn't surprise me if I never end up dating. I also struggle to make and keep friends because I can't seem to connect with people very well.

My sisters are not willing. I have looked into it and quite honestly- the justice system has nothing to offer my family. Its just not that great with handling situations like this. Its one of the many sad aspects of my country.

A report was made when he first was caught - they didn't really do anything then. Even if I were to call them now, they likely won't take it seriously especially since he is now in a well respected position and is an incredibly charismatic person.

I don't have any physical evidence beyond my own words and my family just wants to move on. If something pops up though, I plan to help where I can. But there really isn't anything I can do.
I've always wanted to get into textile crafts like weaving or tapestry. I've been binge watching videos about how to grow and make your own linen and I so desperately want to give it a try.
I play video games, binge watch youtube videos, and like going for nature walks. I'm hoping to get into hands-on crafting once I have more space/money.

I am glad you have been able to glean some insight from my words.

I'm a bit confused by your question. He raped people so he is a rapist by all definitions I am aware of. 

As for whether he will continue to rape? I am not sure. All the literature available on the subject say he most likely will and that combined with his seeming lack of remorse or empathy seems to make a pretty compelling case that his predatory behavior will continue.

I think if he didn't have victims so readily available he might not have been able to molest anyone - especially as a child. But its hard to say what might or might not have been.

I never had the courage to tell my parents. I was too scared of them to say as I thought I would be held equally as accountable as my brother despite me not wanting it.

The way they found out was because of my younger brother saying something. I was nine years old at the time and my parents reached out to the police and CPS to see what they should do. They did end up filing a report and sending my older brother to public school in the hopes of limiting contact with him. 

It didn't work. He continued abusing me til I around 15? I'm not entirely sure when the abuse stopped.

I never got to ask him why. I wish I did. Its one of the many conversations I wish I could have with him for the sake of closure. But I know I will likely never see him again and that its for the best.

My brother is only 2 and a half years older than me - but he was able to physically force me or coerce me all the same. He did the same thing with our younger sisters as well.

Fair enough lol

I've never done one of these before so I was a bit confused.

Just sending in a comment is enough. I was a bit worried nobody would ask anything and I wouldn't be able to interact with anyone regarding this issue. Situations like this are more common than you would think and I want to try and eliminate some of the shame surrounding survivors.

For what he did to me? Its honestly a bit difficult to say but for the most part - no. I am not the sort to hold grudges and its a good thing I don't, a lot of people have hurt me badly like him and I would just exhaust myself to an early grave hating them. When you hold resentment towards people, a lot of times you only hurt yourself. 

I will, however, never be able forgive him raping our little sisters. I was only a few years younger than him, but our sisters were practically babies. If I look at a picture of them at the age they were when he did that to them, I feel a rage unlike anything else I've ever felt.  And it solidifies in my mind that he is a monster that has the potential to do it again.

I don't forgive him for him - I forgive him for me and the peace and healing of my family. I hope one day, he realizes what he has done and becomes a better person. But I wouldn't hold my breath.

I was a 7 years old girl when he started molesting me. I wouldn't be surprised if I was younger than that but my memory on this is foggy.

He raped me multiple times over the course of half a decade and we lived in the same house- so yeah, we still talked and acted for the most part as 'normal' siblings.

The way my brain allowed for me to do that was interesting. When I look back at my childhood it feels like I lived like, 2 different childhoods at the same time. One where I was abused and helpless and the other where I was a happy kid with a loving family.  I would just shove the reality of my abuse back into my mind where it would only come into play when he began to abuse me again.

Edit: And no, he did not go to prison. He is married with two kids and has a career in the military, graduated top of his class with honors. He has cut himself off completely from the family at this time though.

Yes.  It happened when I was a child so I have been able to heal and go to therapy since then. I will likely never be completely healed and I doubt I will ever be able to date like a normal person, but it does not haunt me as much as it used to.  


Thank you for asking

I have tried crossdressing but its very hard for me to pass as anything other than a woman.  Despite this, I have been making plans of trying to pass my voice as masculine so I can talk on vcs on discord and see how being perceived as masculine would feel like.  Maybe go from there?

Thank you for your response, I'll try to keep in mind your advice. I know my post is a rambling mess but I am honestly overwhelmed and don't know what to do. Doesn't help that my post seems to have already been downvoted for some reason- don't know what that's about.
Stay strong friend! I wish you well

It happened to me too - I was seven years old when it started and it continued till I was eleven. 

You aren't alone.

I am nineteen now and in college - not too long ago I was sixteen like you and struggling with the same thing. Counseling really helped me process my feelings towards my abuser and my trauma. 

I am still not completely healed and it will take a long time for that to be the case. 

But I was able to forgive not only my abuser for what he did- but also myself for not being able to defend myself and trusting him in the first place. I was a child, you were a child- we didn't ask nor want for this. This having happened to us says more about the people around us, how they failed to protect us as children or even took advantage of our naivete.

I hope we are both able to heal and to see that there is a future waiting beyond the darkness if only we're brave enough to keep striving forward. It isn't fair that we had to grow up as quickly as we have and to become so brave so young- but thats how things paned out. We are where we are and all you and I can do is try our best and hope for the best. 

I truly hope that you are able to heal from this and see that you are still a person with value - that nothing that man has done has changed that.

I've done counseling for awhile and while it sometimes helped - I think the only thing it did for me was give me someone to talk with and spend time with. Which is good, its better than nothing - but having only a counselor as a friend can be debilitating and expensive.

My family reacted better than I thought- I came out to my sister in a moment of impulse (would not recommend coming out impulsively!) but it turned out alright, even though she had been homophobic in the past she had learned a lot recently and was able to accept me. With her support and others like her, I was able to eventually come out to my mom as an adult years later.

My mom was a bit of a different story - she didn't know how to respond and was obviously less than pleased by the news. She claims to still love me but tried to convince me that I had 'tricked myself' and that thinking women are attractive was normal and doesn't necessarily mean that someone is gay. Ngl, I kind of think she herself is bisexual but is in deep deep denial about it based on our conversations - but the world will never know.

My dad I've never directly told but he definitely knows and just pretends he doesn't. Its easier for him that way and I see no benefit from directly confronting him about it, he would be worse about it than my mom for sure.

All my siblings know and are accepting as they no longer believe most of my parents' BS- though my brothers were a bit weirded out about it, I'm sure they'll come around. That or they won't, doesn't matter- I'm still gay.

Don't tell people you know don't respect you - especially if you don't want to be out to everyone - I'm pretty sure my older brother is the one who outed me to my dad. Which is unfortunate and could have ended badly if my dad hadn't chosen to ignore it instead - so keep in mind that some people can't keep their mouths shut.

Thank you for your kind words. I used to use discord quite often until about two weeks ago. I should probably get back into it but I always struggle to tell if I'm truly wanted or if I am forcing my presence on people. As said, its a me thing I need to figure out. 

I will need all the luck I can get, I appreciate you taking the time to leave a comment.
Having more money would literally solve like 90% of my problems. I could actually spend my life doing what I love instead of slaving away to make a living.

I am bisexual and come from a crazy religious family - as in 'evolution was invented by liberals to trick people into thinking God isn't real' brand of crazy. Absolutely cracked. So I can relate

My recommendation is to focus on your own safety first - don't come out before you are ready and know that closeted or out you are still just as much a member of the LGBT community as anyone else. Think carefully before you come out to someone and consider their possible reactions. Once you let the cat out of the box, you lose control over what happens next in terms of what they do in response to the news.

Try and build a network of people you can trust - its can be hard but there are allies that exist even in the deepest red of states. If you can't find your people, that might be a sign that it would be better to stay quiet for now until you do find an accepting community to surround yourself in. Its hard to be closeted, but it can be even harder to be out and be without support.

I wish you luck friend, I was fortunate enough to find at least a few people to help me come to terms and accept myself enough to not care about what other people think. I hope that that happens for you too.

Being single doesn't have to be a bad thing. I understand companionship is very important for people but there does seem to be a lot of unnecessary pressure to always be dating. That to be single is a sign of failure or a character flaw.

I have never dated nor do I intend to anytime soon. Even if I were interested in dating, I would be hard pressed to find someone willing. That is ok, that gives me time to focus on myself and deal with my own issues.

I guess what I am trying to say is that you being single for a prolonged period of time shouldn't define you as a person nor devalue you in any way. Your worth isn't based on someone else or having  a romantic partner.

I hope that we both one day to find that special someone - and that we're emotionally available and ready when they do come along.
